config.title: inset and position shorthand

intro.title: inset and position shorthand
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple card component that is perfectly centered and sized within its container using the `inset` property. You will learn how `inset` serves as a shorthand for setting `top`, `right`, `bottom`, and `left` values simultaneously, which is especially useful with `position: absolute` or `position: fixed`. The main technologies involved are CSS positioning and the `inset` shorthand property. By the end, you will understand how to position elements precisely and efficiently with fewer lines of code.
intro.usecase: The `inset` property and position shorthand are essential for precisely placing and sizing overlay elements within a container. Developers use these techniques to create full-screen modals, expandable side panels, and tooltips that perfectly align to their parent boundaries. For example, in a dashboard, you might use `inset: 0` to make a loading spinner cover an entire chart panel, or use `inset: 10px 20px` to position a floating filter menu inside a defined area. Mastering these properties ensures UI components are reliably positioned without complex margin or top/right/bottom/left calculations.

objectives: Apply the inset property to position an element relative to its containing block
Configure inset values using shorthand syntax for all four sides
Manipulate element positioning by combining inset with position: absolute
Construct layouts using inset shorthand with position: fixed for viewport-relative placement
Implement inset with position: relative to create offset effects within normal flow
Control element dimensions and positioning simultaneously using inset and position shorthand
Integrate inset property with CSS positioning contexts to create precise alignments

steps.title: Create a container element with position: absolute
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named 'container' and set its position property to 'absolute'.
steps.hint: Use the class selector .container followed by curly braces, then add the position property inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for .container with position: absolute will be created.
successCriteria: The .container class selector exists with position: absolute set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created the .container class with position: absolute.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a CSS rule for .container with position: absolute.

steps.title: Position the container using top, right, bottom, left properties
steps.instruction: Inside the .container rule, set the top, right, bottom, and left properties to 20px each.
steps.hint: Add four separate CSS properties: top: 20px; right: 20px; bottom: 20px; left: 20px;
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will be positioned 20px from each edge of its nearest positioned ancestor.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes top: 20px;, right: 20px;, bottom: 20px;, and left: 20px; properties
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added all four properties: top, right, bottom, and left, each set to 20px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container needs top, right, bottom, and left properties set to 20px each.

steps.title: Introduce the inset shorthand property
steps.instruction: Replace the top, right, bottom, and left properties in your .container rule with a single inset property.
steps.hint: The inset property accepts up to four values (top, right, bottom, left) just like the margin or padding shorthand. Use it to set all four edges at once.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule will use the inset shorthand property instead of separate top, right, bottom, and left properties.
successCriteria: The .container rule contains an inset property with four values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the inset property might be missing some values or not formatted correctly. Make sure it has four values (top, right, bottom, left).
steps.feedbackWrong: The inset property is not present or is incorrect. Replace the top, right, bottom, and left properties with a single inset property.

steps.title: Use inset with a single value
steps.instruction: In the .container rule, change the inset value to a single value of 20px to apply 20px to all four sides.
steps.hint: Replace the current inset value with just '20px' to set the same inset on top, right, bottom, and left.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will be positioned 20px from all edges of its containing element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using a single value like '20px' without multiple values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced the four values with a single '20px' value for inset.

steps.title: Use inset with two values
steps.instruction: Update the inset property in your .container rule to use two values: 20px for vertical (top/bottom) and 40px for horizontal (left/right).
steps.hint: The syntax for two values is inset: vertical horizontal; where vertical sets both top and bottom, and horizontal sets both left and right.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will be positioned 20px from the top and bottom edges, and 40px from the left and right edges of its containing block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using exactly two values: 20px for vertical (top/bottom) and 40px for horizontal (left/right).
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. The step requires using the inset property with two values: 20px and 40px.

steps.title: Use inset with four values
steps.instruction: Update the inset property to use four values: 10px for top, 20px for right, 30px for bottom, and 40px for left.
steps.hint: The four-value syntax is: inset: top right bottom left;
steps.analogousExample:
/* Four-value margin example */
margin: 5px 10px 15px 20px; /* top, right, bottom, left */
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will be positioned with different inset values on all four sides.
successCriteria: The inset property has four values in the order: top, right, bottom, left.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but check the order of values. The four-value syntax should be: top, right, bottom, left.
steps.feedbackWrong: The inset property should have four values in the order: top, right, bottom, left. Try again.

steps.title: Create a second element with position: fixed
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a new class named 'fixed-element' that sets position: fixed and uses the inset shorthand with a single value of 50px.
steps.hint: Define a new CSS selector .fixed-element with the position and inset properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A second CSS rule is added for .fixed-element with position: fixed and inset: 50px.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .fixed-element selector with position: fixed and inset: 50px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both position: fixed and inset: 50px in your .fixed-element rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a new CSS rule for .fixed-element with the correct properties.

steps.title: Create a third element with position: sticky
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a third element with class name 'sticky-element'. Set its position to 'sticky' and use the inset shorthand with a single value of 0.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule starting with '.sticky-element { }' and place the position and inset properties inside the curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A third CSS rule for a sticky element is added, using position: sticky and inset: 0.
successCriteria: The code includes a '.sticky-element' rule with 'position: sticky' and 'inset: 0'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your rule includes both 'position: sticky' and 'inset: 0'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sticky element rule is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added a '.sticky-element' rule with the required properties.

steps.title: Combine inset with other positioning properties
steps.instruction: Add margin: auto to the .container rule to center it within the inset boundaries.
steps.hint: Add the margin property with the value auto inside the existing .container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule now includes margin: auto, which will center the element within the inset-defined area.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added margin: auto inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container rule should include margin: auto to center the element within the inset boundaries.
